scope: Thirteen development cases; no frozen baseline or model quota expansion

subject.text: Our UIKit iOS form has editable name and email fields. Validation is supplied as a callback-based service that takes a snapshot of both strings and eventually returns a dictionary of field IDs to nonempty error messages; an empty dictionary means valid. The callback runs on the main actor but may run immediately, twice, or out of order. A user can edit, cancel, or submit again before it returns. Implement ownership of the pending state and results without replacing the existing fields or losing entered text. Request the first invalid field in name-then-email order, and pass successful snapshots to our save callback, which can itself start another validation. Treat unknown field IDs or empty error messages as a service error. Target iOS 26; include deterministic unit tests without networking or UI automation.

subject.text: Our iOS app uses AVPlayer. We asynchronously load a short description of its current AVPlayerItem through an injected callback on the main actor. Items can be replaced externally, the same item can be inspected again, and results can arrive late or twice. Implement a small owner for loading, success, error, cancellation and no-item states. It must not apply results to a different current item or alter playback preferences. The callback may outlive the owner. Include deterministic unit tests using synthetic player items; no network or UI automation. Target iOS 26.

subject.text: In our AppKit macOS reader, users can read and select the original text normally. Add a custom accessibility rotor for literal search matches, without replacing ordinary text access. Text and query can change while an old search result or rotor is still retained. Search forwards and backwards without wrapping; start at the appropriate end on a fresh search. Text may contain emoji and combining marks; do not select only part of a composed character. Allow overlapping matches only when explicitly requested. Respect the native rotor search filter. Implement this for macOS 26 and unit-test the search callbacks and ranges, without driving VoiceOver.

subject.text: For our AppKit macOS Downloads area, preserve the ordinary Open control and readable status. Give the region and controls useful names, show selection in text as well as accessibility state, and clear stale names and state when reused. Reduced transparency should remove only the backdrop, not content. Keep native AVKit controls and the supplied player. Add a small modal-metadata scope that restores the original flag after repeated begin/end calls. Also implement a custom Notifications checkbox whose ordinary and accessibility press actions share state and respect disabled state. Target macOS 26. Include focused unit tests of configuration and callbacks, not UI automation.

subject.text: Our AppKit app has a custom row containing an ordinary Open button. Rows are reused for different records. Implement explicit row role, title, selection and expansion metadata, while preserving the child button and its contextual name. When a row is rebound, the ordinary action should use the current record ID; disabled actions should not invoke it. Target macOS26 and add unit assertions of metadata and native action dispatch, without UI automation.

In our programmatic AppKit Notifications checkbox, Space, Return and the accessibility press action should use the same on/off transition. The control can be disabled. Show the native responder override and unit tests that pass synthetic key events directly into it; do not use UI automation or require a real window. Target macOS26.
